description: Generate a concise, reviewer-friendly PR description from changelog and branch context; adaptive sections; short by default; no speculation.

instructions: Task: Generate a reliable, reviewer-friendly PR description in Markdown using ONLY the provided changelog and context (no speculation).
Purpose: Enable a human reviewer to quickly grasp what changed, why now, how to verify, and any risks/rollbacks.
Audience: engineers/maintainers (incl. those who don't know the author).
Style: neutral, specific, bullet-first; prefer 150–400 words; no signatures/watermarks.
Title:
- Use context.suggested_title if present; trim to ≤72 chars, imperative, no trailing period.
- Else derive from context.branch: strip prefixes (feature/, feat/, fix/, hotfix/, chore/, refactor/, release/), drop leading ticket IDs, Title Case, ≤72 chars.
Category parsing:
- Parse: feat, fix, refactor, perf, docs, test, build, ci, chore, deps, infra.
- Determine dominant type if clearly most impactful or ≥60% of items; prefix title with [fix]/[feat]/[infra] only if it improves clarity.
Adaptive sections:
- Always include: TL;DR, Impact, Testing, Links, Checklist.
- Include BREAKING only if present.
- Put 'Changes by Category' inside <details> if >5 bullets; otherwise show inline.
- Omit any section that would be empty (except TL;DR).
Short PR mode:
- If ≤3 bullets total and no breaking/migrations, output only TL;DR, Testing, Checklist (+ Links if any).
Content rules:
- Do not restate diffs; explain intent, behavior change, and user-visible effects.
- Call out migrations/flags/API/schema/data impacts in Impact.
- Pair each risk with a concise mitigation or 'None'.
- Extract commands/steps only if present; otherwise minimal steps strictly derived from actual changes.
- If changelog empty/unparsable: say 'No changes detected from provided changelog' in TL;DR; set other sections to 'N/A'.
Output EXACTLY in this Markdown format:

# {Title}

> Base: `{base_branch}` ← Source: `{branch}`

## TL;DR
- What changed: …
- Why now: …
- Status: breaking? migration? flags? (or 'None')

## Impact
- Affected areas/modules: …
- User-visible behavior: …
- Data/schema/API/flags/migrations: … (or 'None')

## BREAKING
- … (include only if applicable)

## Testing & Validation
```bash
# Commands or steps for reviewers (from changelog when available)
```
- New/updated tests: … (or 'N/A')

<details>
<summary>Changes by Category</summary>

### Features
- …
### Fixes
- …
### Refactors / Perf / Infra / Build / CI / Docs / Tests / Chore / Deps
- …

</details>

## Deployment & Rollback
- Deploy: … (or 'N/A')
- Rollback: … (or 'N/A')

## Screenshots / Before–After (optional)
- … (include only for UI/UX changes; otherwise omit)

## Links & Artifacts
- Fixes/Closes: #… (if any)
- Issues/Tickets/Docs/Pipelines: … (or 'N/A')

## Checklist
- [ ] Builds green
- [ ] Tests added/updated
- [ ] Docs updated (if user-visible change)
- [ ] Feature flag default reviewed (if used)
- [ ] Migration tested/applied (if any)
Validation before output: ensure every bullet originates from the provided changelog/context; no fabricated content.

description: Generate a single Conventional Commit message from provided diff context, aligned with git-cliff.

staged_files.description: Output of `git diff --staged --name-only` or equivalent (already provided as context)

git_cliff_config.description: Contents of cliff.toml for commit_parsers alignment

instructions: Output EXACTLY one Conventional Commit message (no extra text). Use ONLY the provided context; do not run commands or speculate.
Subject format: type(scope?): description
- type ∈ allowed_types (lowercase; trim/normalize commas/spaces).
- scope optional; if obvious from staged_files top-level folder/module (e.g., ui, api, core, docs, build, ci, db, infra), include it; otherwise omit.
- description: imperative, specific, ASCII, ≤72 chars, no trailing period.

Quick type heuristic (pick the first that clearly applies from diff_summary + staged_files): fix → bug/error/regression; feat → new capability/API/CLI/endpoint/schema; refactor → non-behavioral restructure; perf → speed/memory; docs → only docs; test → only tests; build/deps → build scripts or manifests/lockfiles; ci → pipelines/workflows; otherwise chore.
Breaking changes: if present in diff_summary/context, use type! or type(scope)! and add a footer line: 'BREAKING CHANGE: …'.
Optional footers: include 'Refs: #123' or 'Closes: #123' only if such references are present in the provided context.
Alignment: ensure the chosen type and shape match commit_parsers patterns in git_cliff_config.
Return format (no commentary):
type(scope): short imperative summary
Optional body (only if strictly needed).
Refs: #123
BREAKING CHANGE: details
